subject: Re: Sparkbridge - data disposition & per-tenant log deletion process
messages:

Cc: Lara Price <lara.price@sparkbridge.com>

Subject: Data disposition question + evidence for procurement

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Sparkbridge has a couple of follow-ups before we can sign the ordering doc: they want a clear description of how customer audit logs and inference request logs are retained and deleted, and a sample deletion attestation we can present to our legal team.

Specific asks:
- What is the default retention for request logs and debug traces in the hosted API? Are there separate buckets for tenant logs vs. platform telemetry?
- Can you confirm how permanent deletion works (S3 delete markers, versioning, or tombstones)? We need to show that data is not recoverable after the retention window if the tenant requests deletion.
- Is there a process for temporary preservation when a legal hold is requested? How is that tracked/audited?

We also need SOC 2 / SIG pointers that map the above controls. Our counsel (copied) will want an example attestation/certificate after deletion. Can you share a sample deletion certificate and any relevant SOC 2 extract that maps to retention/deletion controls?

Thanks,
Evan
Security & Privacy
Sparkbridge

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data disposition question + evidence for procurement

Hi Evan — great to hear from you and congrats on moving to procurement. I've summarized answers below and attached a SOC 2 excerpt and a small sample export you can hand to legal.

Short answers up front:
- Default request logs retention: 30 days for per-request debug traces by default; aggregated usage metrics are kept for 13 months. Tenant-scoped request logs are logically separated into per-tenant S3 prefixes.
- Deletion mechanism: For hosted deployments we use S3 with versioning enabled and lifecycle rules. Deletion requests create a coordinated flow: object-level delete + creation of a signed deletion-transaction record in our audit ledger. For customers that require irrecoverable erase (e.g., regulated PII tenants) we perform object overwrite + delete marker purge within a documented windows (see below).
- Legal hold: we have a documented preserve flag which Support/Legal can enable per-tenant. While preserve is active, lifecycle rules are suspended and a hold entry is recorded in the audit ledger with reasons and TTL.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2027.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary pages 12-16), sparkbridge_log_export_sample.csv (sample rows with redacted values), deletion_cert_template.docx (a fillable attestation template).

Longer explanation (for legal/procurement):
1) Storage & separation
- Tenant logs are written to tenant-prefixed S3 URIs with server-side encryption (KMS) and are logically separated from platform telemetry. Access controls are role-based and audited via CloudTrail.

2) Deletion workflow
- Standard deletion request: Creates a ticket and schedules a lifecycle transition to INTENDED-DELETE. We keep a deletion-transaction record for 90 days in our immutable audit ledger (append-only, backed by WORM storage) so we can prove the delete happened.
- Irreversible erase: For customers who require non-recoverability, we run an overwrite job on objects (single-pass crypto-shred of object content) and then purge versions and delete markers. This is performed during a maintenance window and recorded in the audit ledger; note this adds operational lead time (typically 5–10 business days depending on dataset size).

3) Legal hold
- Legal or a support escalation can set a preserve flag on the tenant. That flag prevents lifecycle transitions and triggers a daily snapshot to a preserved bucket with restricted access. The preserve entries include a reason, owner, and expiration (if provided).

4) Evidence mapping (SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ)
- SOC 2: report pages attached highlight CC6/CC7 controls related to data disposition and logging.
- SIG: we can map specific questions to our retention policies; I can produce a short SIG mapping doc.

Action items I will take:
- Share SOC 2 excerpt and sample export (attached).
- Create a deletion-certificate draft for you to pass to legal (attached template).
- Open an internal runbook task for our engineering team to document the erase lead-time for datasets >100GB.

Marissa / Priyom — looping you in to confirm the technical details above and to create the ERASE runbook ticket (ENGINF-2847). Priyom, can you confirm the 5–10 business day estimate for an irrecoverable erase for tenants of Sparkbridge's size?

Best,
Priya
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2027.pdf, sparkbridge_log_export_sample.csv, deletion_cert_template.docx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data disposition question + evidence for procurement

Thanks for the ping. Confirming the operational details here:

- For hosted customers: we enable S3 versioning and a lifecycle policy that transitions non-current versions to GLACIER and then deletes after the configured TTL. For an "irrecoverable erase" we run an overwrite + purge of versions. The overwrite uses a one-pass secure delete, and we rotate the tenant-specific KMS DEK first when higher assurance is requested.
- Lead time: 5–10 business days is accurate for datasets in the 10–500GB range; for >1TB we recommend scoped planning and additional compute for the overwrite job.
- Audit evidence: after completion we publish a deletion transaction record (signed, with timestamp and job id) and can export the ledger entry as CSV or PDF.

I'll create the ENGINF-2847 ticket and add a small runbook that lists the CLI steps and the required request fields (tenant_id, date_range, preserve_flag false, authorized_by).

- Priyom

1) For the deletion certificate: can Redwood commit to a template timeline for the completion of the erase once customer provides signed authorization? We would like a maximum SLA for completion in the order form if possible.
2) During a preserve/legal hold, can you provide a read-only export of the relevant logs to an S3 location under our control? Our counsel may prefer that copies are preserved under our retention process while Redwood keeps the primary copy on hold.

Also: please confirm whether the audit ledger is immutable for the 90-day proof window and whether Redwood can provide an exported signed copy for litigation support.

Carl, any redlines from BrightLaw?

Lara

Subject: Re: Data disposition question + evidence for procurement

Hi Lara / Evan / Carl — thanks for the clear follow-ups. Quick answers and next steps:

1) SLA for erase completion: We can offer a contractual maximum SLA of 10 business days for tenants with total data under 500GB (we'll include this as an optional appendix to the order form for Sparkbridge). For larger datasets we will agree on a scoped schedule during purchase. That SLA applies to hosted deployments; Dedicated/Private customers may have a different operational flow.

2) Read-only export during hold: Yes — we can copy a daily read-only snapshot of preserved logs to an S3 bucket under your account (cross-account replication with restricted IAM role). That will be done on a cost-recovery basis; we'll add the pricing line item to the appendix.

3) Audit ledger immutability: The 90-day ledger window is backed by WORM storage and we publish signed ledger exports on request. We will provide the signed CSV/PDF with timestamp and job id for litigation support.

Action items we will take now:
- ENGINF-2847: Priyom will create the erase runbook and task.
- Procurement appendix: Marissa will draft the SLA appendix and pricing for cross-account snapshot.
- Deletion cert: I'll send a filled deletion_cert_template once we have authorization from Sparkbridge (attached template is generic).

Carl — if BrightLaw wants to propose redlines to the appendix, please send them and we'll iterate. Evan / Lara — I'll follow up with the formal appendix and the SIG mapping doc by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Priya
